source_refs.title: Delete messages in Gmail - Computer - Gmail Help
source_refs.section: Remove messages from your trash; Learn what happens when you delete a message
source_refs.applicability: Gmail on a computer; time limit stated on the page
source_refs.verified_excerpt: You can recover the message from your trash and move it back to your inbox.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Gmail on a computer: Go to Gmail on your computer. On the left, click 'More', then 'Trash'. Check the box to the left of each message you want to recover. At the top, click 'Move to'. In the 'Move to' menu, choose the folder where you want the messages to go, such as your inbox. When you delete a message in Gmail, it's moved to Trash. Up to 30 days after deletion, you can find the message in Trash. After 30 days, the message is permanently deleted and can't be recovered. Deleted drafts can't be recovered from Trash.

source_refs.title: Email is missing from your Outlook.com inbox | Microsoft Support
source_refs.applicability: Outlook.com web steps; time limit stated on the page
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Messages removed from the Deleted Items folder are recoverable for 30 days.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Outlook.com: Open the Deleted Items folder and check whether the message is there. If it is, select the message and select 'Restore'. If the message isn't in Deleted Items, open that folder. Above the message list, select 'Recover items deleted from this folder'. If you find the message, select it and then select 'Restore'. Messages removed from the Deleted Items folder are recoverable for 30 days.
